title: Private deploy: minimal egress windows and signed-package mirror strategy for air-gapped upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a minimal-risk strategy and acceptance criteria for performing software upgrades in Private/VPC (air-gapped or tightly controlled egress) environments. The goal is to allow customers to perform periodic, short-duration egress windows (or use approved mirror workflows) to fetch signed artifacts and roll out runtime and control-plane updates without violating offline/air-gap constraints or operational SLAs.
background: Customers running Redwood Private frequently operate in regulated networks that prohibit continuous outbound access. Current upgrade options assume either always-on egress or fully offline image import. There is a gap for customers who can allow short, scheduled egress windows or who prefer a signed artifact mirroring workflow. This ticket consolidates requirements, defines a minimal egress window model, and specifies acceptance criteria for mirror tooling and verification checks used during upgrades.
scope_inclusions: Spec for a scheduled egress window flow (timeboxed outbound access) to fetch signed artifact manifests
Design of a signed-package mirror format and a verification pipeline (hash/signature checks) suitable for air-gapped imports
Upgrade orchestration adjustments to support both: an automated egress-window fetch and an offline mirror-import path
Operational guidance and console hooks for admins to schedule and monitor egress windows
Telemetry and audit logging requirements for all artifact fetch and verify steps
scope_exclusions: Implementation of a full CDN or hosted mirror product (we will document supported tools and formats)
Changes to on-prem hardware provisioning or network firewalls beyond config guidance
Automated long-lived inbound tunnels or permanent remote execution agents
non_goals: Replacing existing offline image import APIs (we will interoperate with them)
Introducing new persistent networking proxies that remain open outside scheduled windows
requirements: R1: Egress window orchestration - Admin can declare a timeboxed outbound window (start, duration, CIDR egress endpoints) and the control plane will attempt artifact fetches only during that window

R2: Signed artifact manifest - All packages, container images, and configuration blobs referenced by an upgrade must be accompanied by a verifiable manifest (SHA256 hashes and an RSA/ED25519 signature).
R3: Mirror format - Provide a compact mirror bundle spec (tar + manifest + signature) suitable for air-gapped import via scp/usb or hosted mirror sync tools.
R4: Fetch retry/backoff and partial-resume - The fetch flow must support resumable downloads and deterministic retries to avoid indefinite egress.
R5: Offline verification - Import path must verify signatures and hashes offline and surface a clear validation status before any node changes are applied.
R6: Safety gates - Upgrade orchestration must include preflight checks (disk space, image signature validity, control-plane quorum) and abort on failures with clear rollback guidance.
R7: Narrow egress footprint - Document and minimize the external endpoints and ports required for the egress window; prefer single-host artifact endpoints and well-known ports (443).
R8: Observability - Emit audit events for: window open/close, artifacts fetched, signature validation results, upgrade start/complete/fail. Events must include timestamps and operator identity.
R9: Test harness - Provide automated integration tests that exercise both egress-window fetch flow and offline mirror import flow in CI or a reproducible lab environment.
R10: Admin revoke - Provide an operator control to cancel an in-progress egress window and safely stop ongoing fetches without leaving nodes in an inconsistent state.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Administrator UX - Console and CLI allow creating a scheduled egress window with start time, duration, and allowed destination list; creating, modifying, and cancelling windows is demonstrated in a runbook.

AC-2: Minimal endpoint list documented - Upgrade docs list a single canonical URL and a backup mirror endpoint; network ops can lock down firewall rules to that list and successfully perform an upgrade in staging.

AC-3: Signed manifest validation - During both egress and offline import flows, the system rejects any artifact whose hash or signature does not match the manifest; tests show verification failure prevents node changes.
AC-4: Mirror import verification - A mirror bundle produced by the recommended tooling can be imported offline and validated end-to-end; post-import cluster health is equivalent to online fetch path.
AC-5: Timeboxed behavior - Fetches only occur while the egress window is active; when a window is cancelled, in-progress fetches terminate cleanly and leave no partial upgrades applied.

AC-6: Observability and audit - All fetch and verification events appear in Console logs and audit trail with operator identity and timestamps; sample dashboard shows last 30-day egress-window activity.
AC-7: Rollback safety - Simulated upgrade failures (bad image, insufficient disk) trigger the defined rollback path and cluster resumes prior version without data loss in the test harness.
AC-8: CI tests - Two integration tests run in CI: (a) scheduled egress window upgrade against a staging mirror, and (b) offline mirror import. Both must pass on the release branch before GA.
AC-9: Security sign-off - Security team approves the signed-manifest format and the verification implementation; sign-off documented in ticket links.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Spec + API design and security review (2 sprints). Phase 2: Small beta customers + internal lab validation (1 sprint). Phase 3: Feature flag release to broader private deploy customers with runbook and support playbook (2 sprints). Final: GA after CI gating and security sign-off.
validation_steps: V1: Run the staging upgrade with an allowed egress window and confirm artifacts downloaded and signatures validated
V2: Cancel an in-progress window and verify fetches stop and no partial upgrades applied
V3: Create a malformed manifest in the mirror bundle and verify the import path fails with descriptive errors
V4: Use firewall rules to restrict egress to the documented endpoints and confirm successful upgrade
V5: Check Console audit events for at least 10 recent egress windows and associated artifact events
notes: Prefer leveraging existing offline-import APIs where possible; aim for a manifest format compatible with both container and archive workflows. Coordinate with Security (crypto team) for signature algorithm choice. Schedule a sync with Customer Solutions for beta participants.
